name: The Heavenly Hawaiians
caption: Beat the Springfield Succulents in the promotion's earliest surviving broadcast.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcast of 2 March 1996

name: The Springfield Succulents
caption: Lost to the Heavenly Hawaiians in the promotion's earliest surviving broadcast, then won the inaugural World Women's Tag Team Championship four weeks later.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 2 March and 30 March 1996

name: The Magic Mountain Warriors
caption: Fell short of the inaugural World Women's Tag Team title, then lost to the debuting Faces of Death two weeks later.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 30 March and 14 April 1996

tenures.role: World Tag Team Champions from the Anniversary Bash

name: The Slammer Jammers
caption: Won the inaugural World Tag Team Championship and defended it successfully two weeks later.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 30 March and 14 April 1996

name: The Disciples of Doom
caption: Fell short of the inaugural World Tag Team title, then spent the next season disrupting the North American title picture under manager The Mortician.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 30 March 1996 and 11 January 1997

name: The Glamour Boys
caption: Won a Round Robin tag match in 1996 and a further tag win over Hate and Discontent the following January, managed throughout by Moira Stone.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 14 April 1996 and 11 January 1997

identity.note: A common tag-team name; no document links this team to any other entity billed under the same name.

name: The Faces of Death
caption: Debuted with a win over the Magic Mountain Warriors, then won the World Women's Tag Team Championship from the Cowgirls from Hell the following January.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 14 April 1996 and 11 January 1997

name: The Cowgirls from Hell
caption: Lost the World Women's Tag Team Championship to the Faces of Death in the promotion's own 11 January 1997 broadcast.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcast of 11 January 1997

name: Hate and Discontent
caption: Lost a tag match to the Glamour Boys in the promotion's own 11 January 1997 broadcast.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcast of 11 January 1997

name: The Harlequins
caption: A pair of masked wrestlers whose interference for one another was blamed for costing an opponent a North American title match.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcasts of 2 March 1996 and 11 January 1997

identity.note: A common stable name; no document links this stable to any other entity billed under the same name.

name: The Millionaire Boys Club
caption: Announced by Kevin Kash on the promotion's own broadcast as a high-paying stable auditioning at the promotion's own next pay-per-view.

tenures.source: the promotion's own broadcast of 11 January 1997
